response: {"title":"Falsy-value separation","intervention":"At every edited input check or defaulting expression, separately exercise None, False, numeric zero, empty string, and empty container, and preserve the repository-specified return or exact exception class and message for each instead of treating them as one falsy case.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, this falsy-value separation will improve held-out boundary and invalid-input pass_rate on matched Python tasks under the same deadline, with wall_time and turns captured as costs.","mechanism":"Python truthiness collapses semantically distinct sentinels, values, and container boundaries; forcing separate witnesses exposes incorrect `if not x`, `x or default`, and bool-as-int behavior before it spreads across modules.","assumptions":["At least some affected APIs distinguish among falsy inputs.","Intended behavior for each falsy category is recoverable from code, tests, callers, or documentation.","The small fixed corpus is relevant to edited checks."],"risks":["Some APIs intentionally unify all falsy inputs, making the checks redundant.","The fixed corpus can distract from non-falsy boundaries such as maximum sizes.","Empty custom objects may have domain-specific truthiness not covered by the corpus.","Exact-message expectations may be ambiguous or version-sensitive."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python repair tasks to this appended instruction or no appended instruction with identical tools, models, and deadlines; score hidden tests separating falsy inputs plus other boundary and exact-error cases.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm achieves higher hidden pass_rate on falsy-separation and overall edge tests while meeting the deadline and without a material increase in median turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":7}
